In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of infinitesimal perturbative calculus on Fock spaces and its probabilistic interpretation.
a new calculus on the Fock spaces that can be interpreted in terms of perturbations by time changes of Wiener and Poissson trajectories.
the study of a calculus on Fock spaces that can be used to describe the infinitesimal perturbation of the trajectories of stochastic processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the calculus introduced here provides a natural and unified approach to the analysis and the study of probabilistic interpretations of the Fock space, in particular to the analysis of the regularity properties of the laws of random variables in the Wiener-Poisson setting.
the operators ∇ ⊗ and ∇ ⊖ are the infinitesimal perturbation operators of random variables by changes of time scale and of time shift in the Poisson and Wiener interpretations, respectively.
the operators ∇ +, ∇ -, ∇ ⊖, ∇ ⊗, and the identity form a complete basis of the algebra of infinitesimal perturbation operators on the Fock spaces.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a new calculus on Fock spaces that is closely related to the classical one, but with a different probabilistic interpretation.
the operators ( ∇ ⊖, ∇ ⊗ ) are a natural generalization of the operators ( ∂ ∂ x, ∂ ∂ t ) in the theory of partial differential equations to the theory of random variables.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the operators ∇ ⊗ and ∇ ⊖ are not selfadjoint, but rather skewadjoint.
the Fock space can be viewed as the space of random variables that are perturbation invariant under time changes.
∇ -, ∇ ⊖, ∇ + and ∇ ⊖ form an algebra of operators that is a natural generalization of the Weyl algebra of the harmonic oscillator to the case of the Poisson and Wiener processes.
